evals.prompt: Decompose this goal into worker tasks: add a dark mode toggle to a React app. List the tasks with their dependencies, worker kind, and whether they can run in parallel or need a stack.
expectations: Produces 2-3 tasks with clear dependency ordering
Task names match [a-z][a-z0-9_-]
Identifies which tasks can run in parallel vs need a stack
Assigns a worker kind to each task

evals.prompt: A worker has been BLOCKED for 6 minutes showing an 'are you sure?' prompt after the unit tests all passed. Read the plan, determine the state, and decide what to do. The plan says: 'task auth-api: add token refresh endpoint, worker: codex, depends on nothing'.
expectations: Identifies the worker state as BLOCKED
Plans to read the pane content first
Either answers the approval question or escalates to the user
Does not nudge a worker that is idle/done

evals.prompt: A worker's task failed three times. First attempt: test failure. Second attempt: wrong file scope. Third attempt: test failure again. What do you do now?
expectations: Recognizes that three strikes have been reached
Captures a wiki blocker with what was tried and why it failed
Links the blocker to the task decision
Escalates to the user instead of trying a fourth time

evals.prompt: You are orchestrating two workers: one adding a backend migration (migration 042), another adding an unrelated feature (migration 043). Both PRs are open. The user asks 'can I merge these?' What do you tell them?
expectations: States an explicit merge order by migration number (042 before 043)
Warns about the CI guard and renumbering risk if the higher one merges first
Does not say 'merge anytime'

evals.prompt: A worker reports that its PR is ready and tests pass. Walk through what you do to verify. The orchestrator may not write code.
expectations: Uses gh pr view to check PR state and base branch
Runs the test command in a scratch pane instead of taking the worker's word
Checks the wiki for a handoff capture
Does not merge or ask the worker to merge

evals.prompt: You are about to dispatch two parallel opencode workers in one repo. The plan shows both tasks touching skill directories SKILL.md and evals/evals.json, though for different skills. What do you do before dispatching?
expectations: Computes each task's expected file set and checks wiki claims
Refuses parallel dispatch on the overlap
Chains the tasks as a plain base-branch PR sequence instead
Records the merge order in the wiki

evals.prompt: The bottom PR of a stack has just merged. The next PR's gh pr edit --base main fails: 'Cannot change the base branch because the pull request is part of a stack', and the merge API says it must be merged asynchronously. What did the skill do wrong, and what do you do now?
expectations: Identifies GitHub-native stacks as the cause and says no native stacks should be created
Merges or unpicks using gh stack (checkout/unstack in a scratch worktree)
Retargets the remaining children to main after the parent merge
Commits to plain base-branch PRs for the rest of the effort

evals.prompt: All four self-hosted runners are busy and gates are queued. gh run list shows an in-progress run whose head branch belongs to a PR that was merged yesterday. What does the skill tell you to do now and during prevention?
expectations: Cancels the stale run (scripts/cancel-stale-runs.sh) so gates unblock
Says gate jobs should carry timeout-minutes and a pull_request: closed trigger in the same concurrency group
Does not restart the merged branch's evals for no reason

evals.prompt: A worker opened a non-draft PR, tests green, but the owner says it never showed up for review. gh pr edit --add-reviewer failed with a fine-grained token ('Resource not accessible by personal access token (organization.teams)'). What does the skill say?
expectations: Uses the REST reviewer endpoint (POST requested_reviewers), via scripts/request-reviewers.sh
Verifies the PR actually lists the reviewer afterwards
Says the orchestrator tick re-requests reviewers on any non-draft, unapproved PR lacking one

evals.prompt: You are about to clean up after a merge that returned HTTP 502, and the PR list page is slow. A cleanup script wants to delete the head branch. What does the skill say?
expectations: Refuses to delete until state == MERGED is confirmed via gh pr view
Allows a delay/re-query for API lag
Says a premature delete closes an open PR and loses the branch

evals.title: Capacity guard: refuse dispatch when parallel cap reached
evals.input: Plan three tasks but worker-capacity.toml says max_workers = 1 and one task is already claimed. Should the orchestrator dispatch the second task?
evals.expected_skill_behavior: No. Count active workers before each dispatch; if one more would exceed the capacity (global or per-repo), refuse with 'finish or stop one first'. Do not probe-and-adjust.

evals.title: Model steering from config: per-task override > harness default > fallback
evals.input: worker-capacity.toml defines quick=gpt-5-mini for codex, default=gpt-5-codex, fallback=claude-sonnet-4-5. What model does a 'quick' codex task get? What model does a 'large' claude task get (claude has no per-task overrides, default=claude-sonnet-4-5)?
evals.expected_skill_behavior: quick/codex → gpt-5-mini (per-task wins). large/claude → claude-sonnet-4-5 (harness default). An unknown task-type for claude → claude-sonnet-4-5 (still harness default). For a harness with no default → fallback. Interactive harnesses without {model} in command: model is advisory, stated in brief, not enforced by launch.
